python.title: Python
python.subtitle: Basics to Cloud Automation with boto3

topics.title: Variables, Data Types & Control Flow
topics.why: Every cloud script branches on API responses — solid variable handling and conditional logic are the foundation everything else builds on.
what: Understand Python's built-in types: int, float, str, bool, NoneType
Write if/elif/else chains; use match/case (Python 3.10+) for multi-branch dispatch
Loop over lists and ranges with for; use while with break and continue
Format output with f-strings; understand str() vs repr()
Read and fix common SyntaxError, TypeError, and NameError messages
topics.mini_project: Write a script that reads a number from input, classifies it as positive/negative/zero and even/odd, then prints a formatted summary using f-strings.

resources.name: Python Official Tutorial — An Informal Introduction

topics.title: Functions & Scope
topics.why: Cloud scripts are decomposed into one function per AWS action so each piece can be tested and recomposed independently.
what: Define functions with positional args, keyword args, and default values
Understand local vs global scope; return values instead of relying on globals
Use *args and **kwargs for flexible boto3 wrapper signatures
Write docstrings: what the function does, its params, and what it returns
Decompose a 50-line procedural script into small, single-purpose functions
topics.mini_project: Refactor a temperature converter script into 5+ named functions, each with a docstring and a return value — no bare print() calls inside functions.

resources.name: Real Python — Defining Your Own Functions
Automate the Boring Stuff — Chapter 3: Functions

topics.title: Data Structures: Lists, Dicts, Sets & Tuples
topics.why: boto3 API responses are deeply nested dicts and lists — you must traverse them confidently to extract instance IDs, ARNs, and status fields.
what: Create, index, slice, and mutate lists; understand tuple immutability
Build dicts with literal syntax and dict(); access nested keys safely with .get()
Use sets for deduplication and O(1) membership tests on resource ID collections
Iterate dicts with .items(), .keys(), .values()
Parse a simulated describe_instances response dict and extract specific fields
topics.mini_project: Parse a hardcoded dict that mimics an EC2 describe_instances response and print: instance ID, state, and public IP for each reservation.

resources.name: Real Python — Lists and Tuples in Python

topics.title: List & Dict Comprehensions
topics.why: Comprehensions let you filter lists of AWS resources — all running instances, all buckets in us-east-1 — in one readable line.
what: Write list comprehensions with and without conditional filters
Write dict comprehensions to reshape API response data into lookup maps
Use nested comprehensions sparingly; know when a for loop is clearer
Replace common filter()/map() patterns with equivalent comprehensions
Build generator expressions for memory-efficient iteration over large resource lists
topics.mini_project: Given a list of 10 EC2 instance dicts (with 'state' and 'instance_type' fields), use comprehensions to produce: (1) a list of IDs for running instances, (2) a dict mapping ID to instance_type.

topics.title: File I/O & Exception Handling
topics.why: Cloud scripts read config files, write audit logs, and must handle AWS API errors gracefully without crashing an unattended job at 3 AM.
what: Open, read, write, and append files with the with statement and context managers
Parse and write JSON with json.load() and json.dump(indent=2)
Use try/except/finally to catch specific exceptions: FileNotFoundError, KeyError, ValueError
Raise custom exceptions with informative messages for caller-side handling
Implement simple retry logic for transient IOErrors
topics.mini_project: Write a script that reads a JSON config file (AWS region + bucket name list), validates its structure, performs a dry-run action on each entry, and writes a timestamped results log — with try/except on every file operation.

resources.name: Python Docs — Reading and Writing Files
Real Python — Python Exceptions: An Introduction
Real Python — Working with JSON Data in Python

topics.title: Modules, pip & Virtual Environments
topics.why: Every real cloud project uses third-party packages — knowing how to isolate and manage them is non-negotiable for professional work.
what: Import from the standard library: os, sys, pathlib, json, datetime, time
Create and activate a virtual environment with python -m venv .venv
Install packages with pip; pin versions in requirements.txt
Understand the __name__ == '__main__' guard for importable scripts
Structure a two-module project (config.py + main.py) with clean imports
topics.mini_project: Create a venv, install boto3 and python-dotenv, write requirements.txt, and build a two-module project where config.py loads env vars and main.py imports and uses them — without any hardcoded values.

resources.name: Real Python — Python Virtual Environments: A Primer
Python Packaging User Guide — pip and venv

topics.title: OOP: Classes, Methods & Inheritance
topics.why: boto3 resource interfaces are object-oriented; understanding OOP lets you write clean AWS client wrappers and read SDK source when docs fall short.
what: Define classes with __init__, instance attributes, and instance methods
Understand self; distinguish class attributes from instance attributes
Implement __str__ and __repr__ for readable debug output
Use inheritance to create a specialized class from a base AWS client wrapper
Apply @property and @staticmethod decorators appropriately
topics.mini_project: Build an EC2Manager class with methods: list_instances(), start_instance(id), stop_instance(id), get_instance_state(id) — using hardcoded mock data now, swapped for real boto3 calls in Phase 3.

resources.name: Real Python — Object-Oriented Programming in Python 3

topics.title: JSON & YAML Processing
topics.why: CloudFormation templates are YAML, boto3 responses are JSON — fluent parsing of both is a daily cloud engineering skill.
what: Use json module: loads/dumps with indent, sort_keys, and default for non-serializable types
Install and use PyYAML: yaml.safe_load() and yaml.dump() — always use safe_load
Navigate deeply nested structures with chained .get() calls and default values
Validate a JSON document against a schema using the jsonschema library
Convert between JSON and YAML programmatically
topics.mini_project: Write a script that reads a CloudFormation template (YAML), extracts all resource logical IDs and their types, counts them by type, and writes a JSON summary report.

resources.name: Real Python — Working with JSON Data in Python
Real Python — YAML: The Missing Battery for Python

topics.title: HTTP Requests with the requests Library
topics.why: Cloud engineers call REST APIs constantly — health checks, Slack webhooks, GitHub integrations — requests is the standard tool for all of them.
what: Make GET, POST, PUT, DELETE requests; check status codes and call raise_for_status()
Pass headers (Authorization, Content-Type) and JSON payloads
Handle connection timeouts and implement retry with exponential backoff
Use requests.Session() for persistent connections and shared headers
Parse JSON responses; handle non-JSON error bodies gracefully
topics.mini_project: Write a monitor script that polls a public health-check URL every 30 seconds, logs results to a file, and sends a Slack webhook notification if it returns a non-200 status — with timeout and retry on connection errors.

topics.title: CLI Scripts with argparse
topics.why: Professional automation scripts accept arguments from the command line — argparse makes your tools feel like first-class CLIs, like the AWS CLI itself.
what: Define positional and optional arguments with type conversion and choices
Add subcommands (mycloud ec2 start) using add_subparsers()
Set required vs optional flags; provide helpful metavar and description strings
Validate input inside the parse step and emit clean error messages
Generate automatic --help text that documents every argument
topics.mini_project: Build mycloud.py with subcommands: ec2 list, ec2 start --id, ec2 stop --id, s3 list-buckets — using argparse, with mocked responses printed as aligned tabular output.

resources.name: Real Python — Build a Command-Line Interface with argparse
Real Python — Comparing Python CLI Libraries

topics.title: Environment Variables & .env Management
topics.why: AWS credentials and API keys must never be hardcoded — loading them from the environment is the correct, secure pattern every cloud team enforces.
what: Read env vars with os.environ[] and os.getenv() with a safe default
Use python-dotenv to load .env files in development without touching production
Add .env to .gitignore; document all vars in a committed .env.example
Use pathlib to build OS-independent config file paths
Understand the AWS credential resolution chain: env vars → profile → IAM role
topics.mini_project: Refactor a script that has hardcoded region, bucket name, and API key strings to load everything from a .env file — with a startup check that raises a clear error listing any missing required variables.

resources.name: AWS Docs — Environment Variables for Credentials

topics.title: Logging & Structured Output
topics.why: Unattended cloud automation must produce machine-readable logs that CloudWatch can ingest and alert on — print() statements are not enough.
what: Use the logging module with DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL levels
Configure a root logger with a FileHandler and StreamHandler
Emit structured JSON logs using python-json-logger for CloudWatch ingestion
Add context to every log line: timestamp, script name, AWS region, resource ID
Control log level from an environment variable at runtime
topics.mini_project: Instrument a prior exercise script with the logging module — replace all print() calls with appropriate log levels, emit JSON to stdout, and rotate file logs — so CloudWatch Logs can parse them.

topics.title: Regex for Log Parsing
topics.why: Cloud engineers parse VPC flow logs, ALB access logs, and CloudTrail events with regex to extract IPs, request paths, and error patterns at scale.
what: Compile and use re.search(), re.match(), re.findall(), re.sub()
Write patterns for IPv4 addresses, HTTP methods, status codes, and timestamps
Use named capture groups (?P<name>...) for readable, self-documenting extractions
Parse a multi-line log file line by line and accumulate results
Know when regex is overkill and a simple split() or partition() is better
topics.mini_project: Write a script that reads a sample ALB access log file, uses regex to extract timestamp, client IP, HTTP method, path, and status code, then writes a JSON report with counts per status code.

resources.name: Regex101 — Test and Debug Regex Interactively

topics.title: subprocess & the os Module
topics.why: Cloud scripts orchestrate other tools — aws cli, terraform, kubectl, docker — subprocess is how Python drives them.
what: Use subprocess.run() with capture_output=True, text=True, and check=True
Handle CalledProcessError and inspect returncode and stderr
Use shlex.split() to safely tokenize command strings without shell=True
Use os and pathlib: getcwd, makedirs, path.exists, path.join
Understand the security risk of shell=True and when it is actually needed
topics.mini_project: Write a Python wrapper around aws s3 ls that calls it via subprocess, parses the text output, and prints a formatted table of bucket names and creation dates — with a clear error if the AWS CLI is not on PATH.

topics.title: AWS SDK Setup & IAM Authentication
topics.why: Using the wrong boto3 authentication method is a security risk and the most common source of runtime failures in cloud scripts.
what: Install boto3 and configure credentials with aws configure and named profiles
Understand the credential resolution chain: env vars → profile → instance role
Create boto3 clients vs resource interfaces and know when to use each
Use boto3.Session() with a named profile for multi-account scripts
Call sts.get_caller_identity() to verify which identity a script is running as
topics.mini_project: Write a script that accepts a --profile argument, creates a boto3 Session, calls STS to print the account ID and ARN, and lists the first 5 S3 buckets in that account.

topics.title: S3 Operations with boto3
topics.why: S3 is the most-used AWS service — uploading, downloading, copying, and managing objects programmatically is a daily cloud engineering task.
what: Create buckets, list objects, upload/download with put_object and get_object
Set bucket policies; enable versioning and configure lifecycle rules via the API
Generate presigned URLs for secure, time-limited object access
Use S3Transfer for multipart uploads of files larger than 100 MB
Paginate list_objects_v2 correctly using continuation tokens
topics.mini_project: Write a backup script that compresses a local directory to .tar.gz, uploads it to S3 with a timestamped key, lists objects older than 30 days, and deletes them — all via boto3.

resources.name: Real Python — Python, boto3, and AWS S3

topics.title: EC2 Management & Automation
topics.why: Automating EC2 lifecycle — stopping dev fleets at night, enforcing tags, collecting inventory — is a weekly task for cloud engineers.
what: Launch instances with run_instances(): AMI, type, key pair, security groups, user_data
Filter instances with describe_instances() using the Filters parameter
Start, stop, terminate instances; use Waiters to block until state is reached
Tag resources programmatically; write a tagging compliance checker
Snapshot volumes and deregister old AMIs to control costs
topics.mini_project: Write a compliance script that lists all EC2 instances missing a required 'Owner' tag, prints a tabular report, and with --enforce stops any non-compliant instance after a 5-second confirmation prompt.

topics.title: Lambda Functions in Python
topics.why: Lambda is how AWS runs automation code without servers — writing, packaging, deploying, and invoking functions from Python is a core skill.
what: Write a Lambda handler: understand the event and context objects for common trigger types
Package a function and its dependencies into a deployment ZIP
Deploy and update functions with boto3: create_function and update_function_code
Set environment variables and IAM execution roles via the API
Invoke Lambda synchronously and asynchronously from a Python script
topics.mini_project: Write and deploy (via boto3) a Lambda function that triggers on S3 ObjectCreated events, reads the new object, validates its JSON content, and writes a metadata record to a DynamoDB table.

resources.name: AWS Docs — Deploying Lambda Functions as .zip Files

topics.title: Paginators, Waiters & Error Handling
topics.why: AWS APIs return paginated results and throttle requests — scripts that ignore this silently miss resources or crash on large accounts.
what: Use paginators to iterate all pages of any describe_* API call
Use named Waiters to poll until a resource reaches the desired state
Catch ClientError and inspect error['Error']['Code'] for specific handling
Implement exponential backoff for ThrottlingException using tenacity or custom logic
Log every API call with its arguments and latency for debugging
topics.mini_project: Rewrite the EC2 compliance script using paginators (handles accounts with 1000+ instances), Waiters before acting, and exponential backoff on ThrottlingException.

topics.title: CloudWatch Logs & Metrics via boto3
topics.why: Programmatic CloudWatch access replaces manual console searches and lets you build automated health dashboards and alerting pipelines.
what: Query CloudWatch Logs Insights with start_query() and poll get_query_results()
Put custom metrics to a namespace with put_metric_data()
Create and describe metric alarms; update thresholds programmatically
Stream recent log events from a log group to your terminal with filter_log_events()
Export a log group to S3 for long-term archival and Athena querying
topics.mini_project: Write a daily health report script that queries the last 24 hours of a Lambda function's logs for ERROR patterns, counts them, puts a custom CloudWatch metric, and publishes an SNS alert if errors exceed a threshold.

resources.name: AWS Docs — CloudWatch Logs Insights Query Syntax

topics.title: Infrastructure Automation Capstone
topics.why: Combining all boto3 skills into one idempotent provisioner demonstrates you can do the work cloud engineers do on day one.
what: Design a script that provisions a full environment from a YAML config: VPC, subnet, security group, EC2, S3 bucket
Make it idempotent: check for existing resources by tag before creating
Add --teardown flag that deletes all resources in reverse dependency order
Log every action as structured JSON; implement rollback on any failure
Write a README with required IAM permissions and example config YAML
topics.mini_project: Build env_provisioner.py: reads config.yaml, spins up VPC + EC2 + S3, waits for the instance to pass status checks, and writes outputs.json with public IP and resource IDs.

bash.title: Bash
bash.subtitle: Shell Scripting for Cloud & Linux Environments

topics.title: File System, Navigation & Permissions
topics.why: Cloud engineers SSH into Linux servers constantly — moving around, reading files, and fixing permissions is the minimum viable skill for any hands-on work.
what: Navigate with cd, ls -la, pwd, find, tree; understand relative vs absolute paths
Manage files: cp, mv, rm, mkdir -p, touch, ln -s
Read and set permissions with chmod (octal and symbolic) and chown
Understand the execute bit on scripts and why chmod +x matters
Use find with -name, -type, -mtime, -exec for locating config files and logs
topics.mini_project: Write a script that finds all .log files older than 7 days in /var/log, compresses each with gzip, moves them to an archive directory, and prints a summary of space recovered.

resources.name: The Linux Command Line — Chapter 3: Exploring the System

topics.title: Variables, Quoting & Parameter Expansion
topics.why: Incorrect quoting is the #1 source of Bash bugs — a variable with a space in it will silently break commands in production scripts.
what: Declare and reference variables; understand word splitting with unquoted variables
Use double quotes for variables, single quotes for literals; know when each applies
Apply parameter expansion: ${VAR:-default}, ${VAR:?error}, ${VAR#prefix}, ${VAR%suffix}
Use command substitution: VAR=$(command) over the deprecated `backtick` form
Understand $0, $1..$9, $@, $*, $#, $?, $$ special variables
topics.mini_project: Write a script that accepts a filename argument, validates it is non-empty and the file exists, then prints its line count, word count, and size — using parameter expansion for defaults and error messages.

topics.title: Conditionals: if, test & case
topics.why: Scripts must check if a service is running, if a file exists, or if an AWS CLI command succeeded — conditionals are how you act on those checks.
what: Write if/elif/else with [[ ]] test expressions
Test file conditions: -f, -d, -e, -r, -w, -x, -s
Compare strings with =, !=, =~; compare integers with -eq, -ne, -lt, -gt
Check exit codes: if command; then ... fi and the && / || short-circuit operators
Use case statements for multi-branch dispatch on string values
topics.mini_project: Write a service-check script that tests if nginx is running, if its config directory exists, and if port 80 is in use — printing a color-coded status summary for each check.

resources.name: Ryan's Bash Scripting Tutorial — If Statements

topics.title: Loops: for, while & until
topics.why: Iterating over a list of servers, buckets, or regions to run the same operation on each is a routine cloud automation pattern.
what: Write for loops over lists, arrays, ranges with {1..10}, and command output
Loop over file globs: for file in /path/*.conf; do ...; done
Use while read line to process file output line by line (the safe pattern)
Use until and while true with break for polling loops
Control iteration with break and continue
topics.mini_project: Write a script that loops over a list of EC2 instance IDs (read from a file), calls aws ec2 describe-instance-status for each, and writes a CSV report with instance ID and status.

topics.title: Functions & Script Structure
topics.why: Well-structured scripts with functions and a consistent layout are maintainable — you will revisit scripts written months ago when something breaks at midnight.
what: Define and call functions; understand local variable scoping
Use return codes (not echo) to signal success/failure from functions
Add a shebang (#!/usr/bin/env bash), set -euo pipefail at the top of every script
Write a usage() function and trap EXIT to clean up temp files
Organize scripts: constants at top, functions in the middle, main() at the bottom
topics.mini_project: Refactor a 60-line flat script into a structured script with: a usage() function, a main() function, 3+ named helper functions, set -euo pipefail, and an EXIT trap that removes temp files.

topics.title: Pipes, Redirection & Process Substitution
topics.why: The Unix pipe model is the core of shell power — combining small commands into pipelines is how you process cloud CLI output without writing scripts.
what: Redirect stdout, stderr, and both: >, >>, 2>, 2>&1, &>
Pipe stdout between commands; understand that pipes create subshells
Use /dev/null to silence output; use tee to log and continue a pipeline
Apply process substitution: diff <(command1) <(command2)
Use here-strings (<<< text) and here-docs (<< EOF) for inline input
topics.mini_project: Write a one-liner pipeline that: lists all running processes, filters for a pattern, extracts the PID column, sorts numerically, and writes output to both stdout and a log file simultaneously using tee.

resources.name: The Linux Command Line — Chapter 6: Redirection

topics.title: grep & Regular Expressions
topics.why: Searching logs, configs, and command output with grep is the most-used text operation in any cloud engineer's day.
what: Use grep with -i (case-insensitive), -r (recursive), -n (line numbers), -l (filenames only)
Write basic regex: character classes, quantifiers, anchors, alternation
Use -E (ERE) for extended regex: +, ?, |, grouping ()
Use -P for Perl-compatible regex when you need lookaheads or named groups
Combine grep with pipes to filter multi-step command output
topics.mini_project: Write a log analysis pipeline using only grep, sort, and uniq that: finds all ERROR lines in a log file, extracts the error code, counts occurrences of each, and outputs the top 10.

topics.title: sed for Text Transformation
topics.why: sed is how cloud engineers patch config files in place, strip comments, and transform CLI output in deployment scripts.
what: Use s/pattern/replacement/flags for in-place substitutions in files and pipelines
Edit files in place with sed -i (or sed -i '' on macOS)
Delete lines matching a pattern with d; print specific lines with p and -n
Use address ranges: line numbers, patterns, and ranges like /start/,/end/
Chain multiple expressions with -e or semicolons
topics.mini_project: Write a script that takes a .env.template file and substitutes all {{VARIABLE}} placeholders with values from environment variables using sed, writing the result to a real .env file.

topics.title: awk for Structured Data
topics.why: awk extracts specific columns from tabular CLI output — aws cli, ps, df, netstat — which is a constant need when scripting.
what: Use awk '{print $1, $3}' to extract specific fields by position
Set the field separator with -F for CSV, TSV, colon-delimited files
Use BEGIN and END blocks for headers and summaries
Filter rows with conditional expressions: awk '$3 > 100 {print $0}'
Accumulate totals: sum += $4; print in END block
topics.mini_project: Parse the output of aws ec2 describe-instances --query with awk to produce a tab-delimited report of instance ID, type, state, and launch time — no Python, no jq.

topics.title: Process Management & Job Control
topics.why: Cloud engineers manage long-running processes on servers — starting, backgrounding, monitoring, and killing jobs is a daily operational skill.
what: View processes with ps aux, top, and htop; filter with grep
Send signals: kill -9 (SIGKILL), kill -15 (SIGTERM), kill -HUP (reload)
Background jobs with & and manage with jobs, fg, bg, disown
Use nohup and screen/tmux to keep processes alive after SSH disconnect
Find what is using a port with lsof -i :PORT and ss -tulnp
topics.mini_project: Write a process watchdog script that checks if a named process is running every 30 seconds, logs the check, and restarts it (via a configurable command) if it has died — running itself in the background via nohup.

DigitalOcean — How to Use ps, kill, and nice

topics.title: SSH, SCP & Key Management
topics.why: SSH is the primary interface to every cloud server you will ever manage — mastering keys, config, and tunnels removes daily friction.
what: Generate and manage key pairs with ssh-keygen; understand RSA vs ED25519
Configure ~/.ssh/config with Host entries for alias, IdentityFile, and port
Use SCP and rsync for copying files to and from remote hosts
Set up SSH agent forwarding for jump hosts and bastion servers
Create local and remote port tunnels with -L and -R flags
topics.mini_project: Configure a ~/.ssh/config with 3 server entries (web, db, bastion), copy a deployment package to the web server using rsync over SSH, and set up a tunnel to access the DB server's admin interface locally.

resources.name: SSH Academy — SSH Keys and Config
DigitalOcean — How to Configure SSH Key-Based Authentication

topics.title: Cron Jobs & Task Scheduling
topics.why: Scheduled scripts run cloud housekeeping tasks — nightly backups, log rotation, cost reports — without human intervention.
what: Write cron expressions for common schedules: daily, hourly, weekday-only
Edit the crontab with crontab -e; list and remove jobs with -l and -r
Redirect cron stdout and stderr to log files within the job definition
Use MAILTO= to suppress cron email or send failure output
Use @reboot to run a setup script on instance start
topics.mini_project: Schedule the S3 backup script from Phase 2 to run every night at 2 AM, redirect all output to a log file, and add a second cron job that rotates that log file weekly.

resources.name: DigitalOcean — How to Use Cron to Automate Tasks
The Linux Command Line — Chapter 12: Scheduled Tasks

topics.title: Package Management & systemd
topics.why: Setting up a fresh EC2 instance or container requires installing software and managing services — both are done via package managers and systemd.
what: Use apt (Debian/Ubuntu) and yum/dnf (Amazon Linux/RHEL): install, remove, update, search
Write a server bootstrap script using apt-get -y and DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
Manage services with systemctl: start, stop, restart, enable, disable, status
View service logs with journalctl -u service-name -f
Write a basic systemd unit file to run a custom script as a service
topics.mini_project: Write a bootstrap.sh script that installs nginx, node, and awscli on a fresh Ubuntu instance; enables nginx on startup; and writes a custom systemd service for a Node app.

topics.title: AWS CLI Scripting
topics.why: The AWS CLI is the Bash-native way to drive AWS — combining it with shell constructs lets you automate the console without any Python.
what: Configure profiles with aws configure; switch profiles with AWS_PROFILE
Use --output text, --output json, and --query (JMESPath) to shape output
Combine aws cli calls in loops: iterate over resource lists and act on each
Check exit codes from aws commands to handle errors in scripts
Use --dry-run on supported commands to test without side effects
topics.mini_project: Write a shell script that lists all EC2 instances tagged with Environment=dev, stops each one, waits for stopped state, and logs each action with a timestamp — using only aws cli, loops, and conditionals.

resources.name: AWS Docs — AWS CLI Command Reference

topics.title: jq for JSON Parsing
topics.why: AWS CLI returns JSON — jq is the standard tool for extracting, filtering, and transforming that JSON in shell scripts.
what: Navigate JSON with . (identity), .key, .array[], .array[0:3]
Filter arrays with select(): .[] | select(.state.Name == "running")
Extract and reshape with map(), to_entries, from_entries
Format output with @csv, @tsv, @sh for use in shell variables
Combine aws cli + jq in pipelines for common operations
topics.mini_project: Write a jq-powered pipeline that takes aws ec2 describe-instances JSON output and produces a shell-safe list of public IPs for all running instances — ready to iterate over in a for loop.

resources.name: DigitalOcean — How to Transform JSON Data with jq

topics.title: Environment Bootstrap Scripts
topics.why: Bootstrap scripts run as EC2 user-data or during container builds — writing them correctly means every new instance is configured identically without manual steps.
what: Write idempotent setup scripts: check before installing or configuring
Export variables for child processes; source shared config files
Install software, pull secrets from AWS Secrets Manager via the CLI, write config files
Log every step with timestamps; exit on first error with set -euo pipefail
Test bootstrap scripts locally with Docker before using as EC2 user-data
topics.mini_project: Write a bootstrap.sh that installs dependencies, pulls a DB password from Secrets Manager, writes a .env file, and starts the app service — idempotent enough to run twice without side effects.

AWS Docs — Secrets Manager CLI Examples

topics.title: Log Monitoring & Alerting Scripts
topics.why: Cloud engineers build lightweight monitoring scripts to catch issues before full observability tools are in place or for custom alert conditions.
what: Tail and watch log files with tail -f and while read
Use grep with real-time output to detect error patterns and fire alerts
Send Slack webhook notifications from Bash using curl and JSON payloads
Track state between script runs using a small state file
Schedule with cron and handle the case where the script is already running (lockfile)
topics.mini_project: Write a log watcher that tails nginx error.log, counts CRITICAL entries per minute, and sends a Slack webhook alert with the count and last error line when it exceeds a configurable threshold.

resources.name: DigitalOcean — Using Curl to Send HTTP Requests

topics.title: Deployment & Rollback Scripts
topics.why: Reliable deployment scripts with automated rollback mean a bad release is a 2-minute recovery instead of a 2-hour incident.
what: Write a deploy script: pull artifact, run pre-deploy checks, swap symlinks atomically
Record the previous version to a VERSION file before deploying
Implement --rollback mode that restores the previous symlink in one command
Add a health-check loop after deployment: curl the endpoint until success or timeout
Lock the deploy with a lockfile; clean up the lock on EXIT via trap
topics.mini_project: Build deploy.sh that: pulls a release tarball from S3, extracts to a timestamped directory, symlinks /app/current to it, runs a health check, and rolls back the symlink automatically if the health check fails.

topics.title: Health Check & Infrastructure Validation Scripts
topics.why: Cloud engineers run validation scripts after every deployment or infrastructure change to confirm the environment is healthy before declaring success.
what: Check HTTP endpoints with curl: status code, response body pattern, response time
Verify services are running: systemctl is-active, lsof port checks
Validate AWS resources: check security group rules, verify S3 bucket accessibility
Aggregate check results and exit with code 0 (pass) or 1 (fail) for CI integration
